unite_adi: UPPER SECONDARY-YEAR 12 (AFTER PREP)-LEVEL: B2.4 - THEME 5: LIFE IN THE NEIGHBOURHOOD, CITY & SOCIAL LIFE

bolumler.ogrenmeKanitlari: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: Students will organise a charity event to support a local community cause by taking on roles such as planners, coordinators, and participants. Students will begin by identifying a social issue in their neighbourhood such as supporting a food bank or organising a park clean-up. Then, they will create a plan, divide responsibilities, and work together to prepare for the event. Each student will explain the purpose of their initiative in terms of how it helps the community, and how it encourages teamwork, responsibility, and kindness. The event may include activities like donation sales, or community clean-ups. Finally, they will share their experience through a report, photos, or a simple presentation, discussing their roles, challenges, and the impact on their community. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme. Öğrenme-Öğretme Yaşantıları
bolumler.temelKabuller: This theme includes the concept of ''life in the neighbourhood, city and social life with its components such as architecture and design in cities; volunteerism in social communities'' and it is assumed that it could be present in almost all languages, with some exceptions. It is assumed that a student in after prep year 12 of upper secondary school may know what architecture and design in cities; volunteerism in social communities mean in their as it is known that almost all people who start to learn a new language bring their pre-existing knowledge (in their own language) with them and transfer it to their new language learning context. However, they may not know how to say these things in a foreign language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. Fortunately, this existing knowledge in their own language can help them recognise, understand, and learn them more easily in a foreign language, in this case English. As they are students in after prep year 12 of upper secondary school, they are expected to know some basic vocabulary about ''life in the neighbourhood, city and social life'' and also some necessary structures in English from the previous themes and/or years. These grammar items and vocabulary are revised during the ''Revision Programme'' at the beginning of the year, and they can be used as a basis for learning the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme, so that the new grammatical elements in the current theme can be learnt easily.
bolumler.onDegerlendirme: It is assumed that these students in after prep year 12 of upper secondary school are ready to learn the concept of ''life in the neighbourhood, city and social life with its components such as architecture and design in cities; volunteerism in social communities'' cognitively, affectively, and socially since it is appropriate to their age and language level. Therefore, a contextual poster or a large picture could be provided for the students to remember and practise the items that they are related and previously learnt so that they can discuss about the poster and/or the picture in pairs and write down what they remember. This session can help them revise all the related vocabulary and grammatical elements that they have already learnt from previous themes or from previous years as a preparatory practice. In this way, their performance can be evaluated in terms of how much they remember and how accurately they use these items to build their competence in the current theme. It can help the teacher decide what to emphasise, revise, and practise in order to facilitate the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme. (Their performance can be evaluated by rubrics, a rating scale, and /or a marking scheme during these practices.).
bolumler.zenginlestirme: Objective: To write an essay on architecture and design in the city in English by using target vocabulary and target grammar. Activity 1: Writing an Essay Students work in groups to write an essay comparing two well-known buildings from different time periods in the same city, one historical and one modern. They describe differences in design, materials (such as concrete), and emerging construction methods. The essay includes target vocabulary, such as ''to stand out'', ''to construct'', and ''to refurbish'', along with descriptive terms like ''daring'', ''recognisable'', and ''captivating'', to characterise the buildings. In addition to comparing the structures, students explore the impact of these buildings on the city and its inhabitants, both internally and externally. This activity not only allows students to practice the target vocabulary but also deepens their understanding of how cities are shaped through architectural advancements. After completing the essays, groups present their work to the class. The teacher provides constructive feedback on accuracy, creativity, and the effective use of target vocabulary, grammar, and pronunciation during the presentations. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
bolumler.destekleme: Objective: To create a poster about their favourite architectural piece in English by using target vocabulary. Activity 1: Creating a Poster In this activity, students use architecture and design vocabulary to create a poster about their favourite architectural piece in their city.. They choose a famous building or one from their city and include its name, location, and key features. Students should use target vocabulary, such as ''concrete, construction, urbanisation, interior, exterior, iconic, elegant, unique, recognizable, daring, and lively'', to describe the building. The poster should include a visual or drawing of the building, accompanied by a brief description that focuses on its design and architectural features and explains why it is their favourite. Then, students present their posters to the class. The teacher provides feedback on the use of the target language including target vocabulary, grammar, and pronunciation and also accuracy and creativity. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
